Class TuiView

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.client.view.tui.TuiView
All Implemented Interfaces:
ClientView
public class TuiView extends Object implements ClientView
Text user interface controller for the client application.

This class has two architectural roles:

  • it reads user commands from a Scanner, parses them with TuiCommandParser, and forwards them to the attached ServerProxy;
  • it implements ClientView, so the networking layer can call it when the server sends updates that must be printed on the terminal.

The TUI normally collaborates with two threads. The main client thread runs start() and reads user input. A networking thread may call the ClientView methods when server messages arrive. With TCP, that second thread is the VirtualServerTCP reader thread. With RMI, it is an RMI callback thread.

For this reason, the methods that print output are synchronized: command output and server updates must not write to the terminal at the same time.

  • Method Details

    • attachServerProxy

      public void attachServerProxy(ServerProxy serverProxy)
      Attaches the network-side proxy used to send user commands to the server.

      The proxy must be attached before start() is called.

      Parameters:
      serverProxy - proxy connected to the remote server

    • start

      public void start()
      Starts the blocking input loop of the text user interface.

      The method prints the initial message, then reads one line at a time. Blank lines only redraw the prompt. Non-blank lines are parsed and dispatched to the server proxy. The loop stops when the user enters quit, when a connection error happens, or when the scanner reaches end of input.

      If input ends without an explicit quit, the controller still closes the attached server proxy.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no server proxy was attached before start

    • showError

      public void showError(ErrorPayload payload)
      Prints a server or client error.

      If a game state was already received, the renderer prints it again after the error so the player does not lose the current board context.

    • showGameUpdate

      public void showGameUpdate(GamePayload payload)
      Prints the current game state received from the server.

      The payload is stored as the last known game state. If an error happens during the match, showError(ErrorPayload) can render this state again after the error message.

      Specified by:
      showGameUpdate in interface ClientView
      Parameters:
      payload - current game state to show

    • showFinalGameResult

      public void showFinalGameResult(GamePayload payload)
